prompt: Students should pay their full university fees as they benefit from having university studies and not the society as a whole. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay:
It is often argued that university students should pay the full cost of their education because they are the main beneficiaries, rather than society as a whole. While I agree that students should contribute towards their university fees, I believe that the government should also provide financial support, particularly for students from disadvantaged families.

On the one hand, requiring students who can afford university education to pay their own fees can allow governments to allocate their limited financial resources to other important areas. Running universities requires considerable expenditure on facilities, teaching staff, technology and other educational resources. If financially capable students cover these costs themselves, the government can use the money saved to improve essential public services such as healthcare, transport and infrastructure. This can benefit a much larger proportion of the population. For example, instead of fully subsidising university places for students from wealthy families, a government could use part of this funding to improve public hospitals and transport facilities.

On the other hand, I believe that governments should continue to support students from low-income families. Although these students may have the ability to succeed academically, they may not have enough money to pay for university education. If they are required to pay the full fees, many talented individuals may be forced to abandon higher education. Therefore, providing free or subsidised university education to disadvantaged students can give them equal opportunities to obtain professional qualifications. For instance, a talented student from a poor family could receive government assistance to attend university and later become a teacher, doctor or engineer, thereby contributing to society.

In conclusion, I agree that students who are financially capable should contribute to the cost of their university education, as this can enable governments to spend more on other essential sectors. However, university education should not become inaccessible to students from poor families, and governments should continue to provide them with appropriate financial assistance
